standard_prerequisites.name: Hom-tensor compose identity
standard_prerequisites.use: SheafHom^*(K^*, SheafHom^*(L^*,I^*)) = SheafHom^*(Tot(K^*  otimes  L^*), I^*).

standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of the hom complex
standard_prerequisites.use: H^0 of sections of the hom complex equals homotopy classes.

core_obligations: For an acyclic complex K^*, establish the chain Hom_{K(O_X)}(K^*, SheafHom^*(L^*,I^*)) = H^0(Gamma(X, SheafHom^*(K^*, SheafHom^*(L^*,I^*)))) = H^0(Gamma(X, SheafHom^*(Tot(K^*  otimes  L^*), I^*))) = Hom_{K(O_X)}(Tot(K^*  otimes  L^*), I^*) = 0, with the middle step the compose lemma (proof lines 10504-10529).
The final equality holds because Tot(K^*  otimes  L^*) is acyclic by K-flatness of L^* and I^* is K-injective; conclude K-injectivity of SheafHom^*(L^*,I^*) (proof lines 10530-10533).
proof_roadmap: Chain the hom-tensor identities from the acyclic test complex.
Vanish the final term by K-flatness and K-injectivity.
difficulty_reason: The proof is a four-term equality chain identifying Hom from an arbitrary acyclic complex with Hom from a K-flat tensor product into the K-injective target, which vanishes.
